claim: Intelligent behavior and cognitive functions in mammals depend on cortical microcircuits made up of a variety of excitatory and inhibitory cells that form a forest-like complex across six layers.
source: Intelligent behavior and cognitive functions in mammals depend on cortical microcircuits made up of a variety of excitatory and inhibitory cells that form a forest-like complex across six layers.
evidence: This is a general statement about cortical organization that draws from established neuroscience knowledge.

claim: Existing techniques are limited as to simultaneous monitoring and stimulation at different depths without damaging a large volume of cortical tissue.
source: However, existing techniques are limited as to simultaneous monitoring and stimulation at different depths without damaging a large volume of cortical tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by the discussion of limitations of existing methods throughout the manuscript.

claim: The double-μPeriscope method uses a tiny optical probe consisting of two microprisms mounted on a single shaft.
source: The method uses a tiny optical probe consisting of two microprisms mounted on a single shaft.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and shown in the figures.

claim: Two distinct cortical layers can be optogenetically and independently manipulated using the double-μPeriscope.
source: We demonstrate the versatility of the probe in three sets of experiments: first, two distinct cortical layers were optogenetically and independently manipulated
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in the manuscript with data shown in Figure 1.

claim: One layer can be stimulated while the activity of another layer is monitored using the double-μPeriscope.
source: second, one layer was stimulated while the activity of another layer was monitored
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally with data shown in Figure 2a-d.

claim: The activity of thalamic axons distributed in two distinct cortical layers can be simultaneously monitored in awake mice using the double-μPeriscope.
source: third, the activity of thalamic axons distributed in two distinct cortical layers was simultaneously monitored in awake mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally with data shown in Figure 2e-h.

claim: Optogenetic manipulation has been established as a powerful method to examine the causal relationship between specific cell types and network activity, cognitive functions or animal behavior.
source: Over the last decade optogenetic manipulation – either activation or inhibition – of specific cells (Nagel et al., 2003; Boyden et al., 2005) has been established as a powerful method to examine the causal relationship between the specific cell type and the network activity, cognitive functions or animal behavior (Deisseroth, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational optogenetics papers.

claim: Multichannel electrical recording is the most widely used approach to measure neural responses to optogenetic stimulation.
source: Multichannel electrical recording is the most widely used approach to measure the neural responses to optogenetic stimulation.
evidence: This is stated as a general observation about current practices in the field.

claim: Extracellular signals represent the summation of the activity of all structures (dendrites, axons, and cell bodies) from all cell types surrounding each electrode.
source: The problem with this approach, however, is that extracellular signals represent the summation of the activity of all structures (dendrites, axons, and cell bodies) from all cell types surrounding each electrode
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about extracellular recording properties.

claim: Extracellular activity is usually very complex in vivo, particularly in the awake brain.
source: even worse, extracellular activity is usually very complex in vivo, particularly in the awake brain (Buzsáki, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Buzsáki 2006.

claim: It is extremely difficult to explain why and how every single pattern of extracellular activities is generated.
source: It is extremely difficult to explain why and how every single pattern of extracellular activities is generated.
evidence: This is an inference based on the complexity of extracellular signals.

claim: Recently developed methods permit optogenetic stimulation or calcium imaging of ~50 neurons that are arbitrarily distributed in three-dimensional space.
source: Though most approaches are either limited in range (i.e., the total depth) or speed, recently developed methods permit optogenetic stimulation or calcium imaging of ~50 neurons that are arbitrarily distributed in three-dimensional space (Pégard et al., 2017; Geiller et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent technical papers.

claim: Fast volumetric cortex-wide two-photon imaging at cellular resolution has been developed.
source: as well as fast volumetric cortex-wide two-photon imaging at cellular resolution (Demas et al., 2021; Prevedel et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to technical papers.

claim: Imaging across different cortical depths (z-axis) is more difficult to implement than the more conventional x–y scanning.
source: Imaging across different cortical depths (z-axis) is more difficult to implement than the more conventional x–y scanning.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge about two-photon imaging techniques.

claim: Large (1 mm) prisms covering all cortical layers allow simultaneous imaging of neurons across layers.
source: More invasive approaches using a large (1 mm) prism covering all cortical layers would allow simultaneous imaging to neurons across layers (Chia and Levene, 2009; Andermann et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Significant damage is caused by 1 mm prism insertion into cortical tissue.
source: however, the significant damage caused by 1 mm prism insertion into the cortical tissue must be considered.
evidence: This is inferred from the discussion and supported by citation to Andermann et al., 2013.

claim: Substantial bleeding during surgery is unavoidable with 1 mm prism insertion.
source: Substantial bleeding during surgery is unavoidable and a significant number of cells are killed or damaged by the procedure (Andermann et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Andermann et al., 2013.

claim: A significant number of cells are killed or damaged by 1 mm prism insertion.
source: Substantial bleeding during surgery is unavoidable and a significant number of cells are killed or damaged by the procedure (Andermann et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Andermann et al., 2013.

claim: The repairing process after 1 mm prism insertion may significantly alter the local and long-range connections between survived neurons.
source: Since the repairing process may significantly alter the local and long-range connections between survived neurons, the imaged neuronal network may no longer function in a way the normal healthy network did before the operation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the consequences of tissue damage.

claim: Single tapered fibers with multiple windows can be used for less invasive optogenetic approaches.
source: Less invasive approaches use a single tapered fiber that has multiple windows (Pisanello et al., 2014) or micro-LED probes (Cao et al., 2013; McAlinden et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to technical papers.

claim: Single tapered fibers and micro-LED probes are only capable of optogenetic stimulation and do not permit calcium fluorescence imaging.
source: however, they are only capable of optogenetic stimulation and do not permit calcium fluorescence imaging.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of cited technologies.

claim: A single endoscope with a right-angled microprism can deliver light to and receive light from a single cortical layer simultaneously.
source: A relatively standard approach is the insertion of an endoscope that with the aid of a right-angled microprism can deliver light to and receive light from a single cortical layer simultaneously (Suzuki and Larkum, 2017; Suzuki and Larkum, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Each μPeriscope consists of a 0.10 mm × 0.10 mm or 0.18 mm × 0.18 mm micro right-angled prism, a custom-designed gradient-index (GRIN) lens, and a multimode optical fiber.
source: Each μPeriscope consists of a 0.10 mm × 0.10 mm or 0.18 mm × 0.18 mm micro right-angled prism, a custom-designed gradient-index (GRIN) lens, and a multimode optical fiber.
evidence: This is a direct description of the device components.

claim: ChR2 and YFP were expressed in L5 pyramidal neurons for the experiments.
source: We expressed light-sensitive ion channels, channelrhodopsin 2 (ChR2) (Nagel et al., 2003; Boyden et al., 2005) and yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) in L5 pyramidal neurons (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Combined stimulation of cell body and distal apical dendrites within a close time window induces a large, regenerative, long-lasting calcium plateau potential that evokes a burst of somatic action potentials in vitro.
source: First, a previous in vitro study showed that combined stimulation of cell body and distal apical dendrites within a close time window induces a large, regenerative, long-lasting calcium plateau potential that evokes a burst somatic action potentials (APs) (Larkum et al., 1999)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Larkum et al., 1999.

claim: It remains unknown whether and under what conditions BAC firing occurs in vivo.
source: However, due to technical difficulties, it remains unknown whether and under what conditions BAC firing occurs in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: The double-μPeriscope allowed direct examination of BAC firing in vivo for the first time.
source: The double-μPeriscope, in combination with electrophysiological recordings from L5 allowed us to directly examine this question in vivo for the first time.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach.

claim: Somatic L5 stimulation preceding dendritic L1 stimulation in vivo under anesthesia evoked more prominent deflections of the local field potential compared to stimulation of either compartment alone.
source: In agreement with the previous in vitro data, somatic L5 stimulation preceding dendritic L1 stimulation in vivo under anesthesia evoked more prominent deflections of the local field potential (Figure 1e)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Somatic L5 stimulation preceding dendritic L1 stimulation evoked more APs compared to stimulation of either somatic or distal dendritic compartment alone.
source: and more APs (Figure 1f), compared to the stimulation of either somatic or distal dendritic compartment alone.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Backpropagating AP-induced Ca2+ spike firing occurs in vivo.
source: This result suggests that the backpropagating AP-induced Ca2+ spike firing does occur also in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results shown in Figure 1.

claim: ChR2 and YFP were expressed in L2/3 pyramidal cells in the primary motor cortex using Rasgrf2-2A-dCre mice with Cre-dependent AAV vector with CaMKIIα promotor.
source: by expressing ChR2 and YFP in L2/3 pyramidal cells in the primary motor cortex (Figure 2b) through combined use of a transgenic mouse line Rasgrf2-2A-dCre with Cre-dependent adeno-associated virus vector with CaMKIIα promotor.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The upper μPeriscope stimulated ChR2-expressing L2/3 pyramidal cells while the lower μPeriscope measured calcium fluorescence in L5.
source: The upper μPeriscope stimulated ChR2-expressing L2/3 pyramidal cells while the lower μPeriscope measured the calcium fluorescence in L5 where a cell-permeable synthetic calcium indicator (Cal-590 AM) was preinjected.
evidence: This describes the experimental setup.

claim: The net effect of L2/3 stimulation onto L5 is inhibitory in the motor cortex.
source: In agreement with the recent study in primary somatosensory area using a different approach (electrophysiological recordings) (Pluta et al., 2019), the net effect of L2/3 stimulation onto L5 turned out to be inhibitory in the motor cortex (Figure 2c, d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c, d and citation to Pluta et al., 2019.

claim: L2/3-to-L5 inhibition might be a general principle across the cortex.
source: This result suggests that the L2/3-to-L5 inhibition might be a general principle across the cortex in contrast to the prevailing textbook assumption that L2/3-to-L5 projections are excitatory (Douglas and Martin, 2004).
evidence: This is speculative inference based on the experimental results and comparison to previous work.

claim: The prevailing textbook assumption is that L2/3-to-L5 projections are excitatory.
source: in contrast to the prevailing textbook assumption that L2/3-to-L5 projections are excitatory (Douglas and Martin, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Douglas and Martin, 2004.

claim: Somatostatin-positive interneurons are likely responsible for translaminar inhibition in the somatosensory cortex.
source: The previous study suggested that somatostatin-positive interneurons are likely to be responsible for the translaminar inhibition in the somatosensory cortex (Pluta et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pluta et al., 2019.

claim: The posteromedial thalamic nucleus (POm) sends axons to cortical layers 1 and 5a in the primary somatosensory area.
source: The posteromedial thalamic nucleus (POm) sends axons to cortical layers 1 and 5a in the primary somatosensory area (Figure 2f; Wimmer et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wimmer et al., 2010 and shown in Figure 2f.

claim: It is unknown whether the activities of POm axonal pathways to layers 1 and 5a are same or different.
source: however, it is unknown whether the activities of these two axonal pathways are same or different.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap.

claim: GCaMP6s was expressed in POm using Gpr26-cre transgenic mouse line and Cre-dependent AAV vector.
source: A genetic calcium indicator GCaMP6s (Chen et al., 2013) was expressed in POm using a transgenic mouse line Gpr26-cre (Gong et al., 2007) and a Cre-dependent adeno-associated virus vector encoding GCaMP6s.
evidence: This describes the experimental method with citations.

claim: The axonal activities in layers 1 and 5a are surprisingly variable.
source: We found that the axonal activities in layers 1 and 5a are surprisingly variable; they are clearly uncorrelated in some trials but highly correlated in others (Figure 2g, h).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2g, h.

claim: The mean cross-correlation coefficient between axonal activities in layers 1 and 5a was lower than 0.3 in all four mice.
source: The cross-correlation analysis confirmed this variability, although the mean coefficient was lower than 0.3 in all four mice (Figure 2h)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: POm neurons may deliver different types of information to layers 1 and 5a.
source: suggesting the possibility that POm neurons deliver different types of information to layers 1 and 5a.
evidence: This is speculative inference based on the correlation data.

claim: Multiple bare optical fibers with a flat end have been used to image multiple brain regions.
source: Multiple bare optical fibers with a flat end have been used to image multiple brain regions (Kim et al., 2016; Sych et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The bare optical fiber approach is suitable if the target brain areas are sufficiently separate (>1 mm).
source: However, this approach is suitable if the target brain areas are sufficiently separate (>1 mm)
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the cited approach.

claim: The double-μPeriscope method has significant advantages to investigate structures that are close (<1 mm) such as cortical layers in the rodent cortex.
source: but as shown in the three sets of experiments, our method has significant advantages to investigate more close (<1 mm) structures such as cortical layers in the rodent cortex.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental demonstrations.

claim: Optical fibers with a flat end would need higher pressure and therefore damage the cortical tissue upon insertion.
source: Optical fibers with a flat end would need higher pressure and therefore damage the cortical tissue upon insertion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the physical properties of the devices.

claim: The sharp edge of microprism allows smooth insertion of the probe with significantly less damage.
source: In contrast, the sharp edge of microprism allows us to smoothly insert the probe with significantly less damage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design of the device.

claim: Layer-specific activation/imaging with a downward oriented light beam from a bare optical fiber is problematic.
source: Moreover, layer-specific activation/imaging with a downward oriented light beam from a bare optical fiber is problematic
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of alternative approaches.

claim: Previous studies used an electric lens combined with two-photon microscopy to measure cellular activities at two depths.
source: Previous studies used an electric lens combined with two-photon microscopy (Grewe et al., 2011; Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2019; Francioni et al., 2019) to measure the cellular activities at two depths.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Imaging with electric lens is not simultaneous because the electric shift of focal plane takes time for shifting and stabilization.
source: The limitations of this approach are (1) that imaging is not simultaneous because the electric shift of focal plane takes time for shifting and stabilization
evidence: This is an inference about the technical limitations of the cited approach.

claim: The maximum distance of shift with electric lens is 500 μm.
source: and (2) that the maximum distance of shift is 500 μm
evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation of the cited approach.

claim: Imaging deeper structures with electric lens needs more laser power.
source: A related issue is that imaging deeper structures needs more laser power.
evidence: This is based on knowledge about two-photon imaging physics.

claim: Deep subcortical structures cannot be imaged with electric lens approach unless a substantial amount of overlaying cortical tissue is surgically removed.
source: Besides, deep subcortical structures cannot be imaged with this approach unless a substantial amount of overlaying cortical tissue is surgically removed (Dombeck et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dombeck et al., 2010.

claim: The distance between two μPeriscopes can be freely adjusted.
source: The double-μPeriscope we show here does not have these limitations because the distance between two μPeriscopes can be freely adjusted
evidence: This is a claim about the design flexibility of the device.

claim: Imaging with double-μPeriscope is simultaneous no matter how distant the two μPeriscopes are.
source: and imaging is simultaneous no matter how distant the two μPeriscopes are.
evidence: This is a claim about the capability of the device.

claim: Deep subcortical structures can be imaged or optogenetically stimulated with the double-μPeriscope without substantial damage of cortical tissue.
source: Deep subcortical structures can also be imaged or optogenetically stimulated with the double-μPeriscope without substantial damage of cortical tissue.
evidence: This is a claim about the capability of the device based on its design.

claim: The cost to setup the imaging system with a double-μPeriscope is an order of magnitude less expensive than electric lens approaches.
source: Importantly, the cost to setup the imaging system with a double-μPeriscope is an order of magnitude less expensive.
evidence: This is a claim about the cost advantage of the method.

claim: The double-μPeriscope requires only tiny prisms, GRIN lenses and a high sensitivity scientific camera as the main components.
source: The reason for the significantly lower cost is that it requires only tiny prisms, GRIN lenses and a high sensitivity scientific camera as the main components.
evidence: This describes the components of the system.

claim: Micro-optics can now be 3D printed.
source: Given ever-improving scientific cameras and lowering costs of micro-optics that can now be 3D printed (Gissibl et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gissibl et al., 2016.

claim: The present version of double-μPeriscope uses single-core multimode fiber.
source: The present version of double-μPeriscope uses single-core multimode fiber
evidence: This describes a technical specification of the device.

claim: It is impossible to visualize subcellular structures in the imaged layer with the present version of double-μPeriscope.
source: therefore, it is impossible to visualize subcellular structures in the imaged layer.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitation based on the fiber type used.

claim: A commercially available multicore optical fiber bundle would allow visualization of subcellular structures if spatial resolution is required.
source: However, a commercially available multicore optical fiber bundle would allow this if spatial resolution is required in other applications.
evidence: This is speculation about potential improvements to the device.

claim: Sim1-KJ18-Cre × Ai32 transgenic mouse line was used to express ChR2 in L5 pyramidal neurons.
source: To express ChR2 in L5 pyramidal neurons, a transgenic mouse line Sim1-KJ18-Cre × Ai32 was used.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: The fluorescence reduction in L5 after optogenetic stimulation of L2/3 was statistically significant in Rasgrf2-2A-dCre mice (n = 3 mice, 20 measurements in each mouse, all p < 0.05, two-tailed Student's t-test).
source: Summary of data from Rasgrf2-2A-dCre mice where the fluorescence reduction in L5 after optogenetic stimulation of L2/3 was statistically significant (n = 3 mice, 20 measurements in each mouse, all p < 0.05, two-tailed Student's t-test).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Two-photon imaging of axonal activities at deep layers is still challenging, even at a single focal plane.
source: Compared to cell bodies and dendrites, two-photon imaging of axonal activities at deep layers is still challenging (Broussard et al., 2018), even at a single focal plane, let alone fast sequential imaging at multiple depths.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Broussard et al., 2018.

claim: The double-μPeriscope measured axonal activities in cortical layers 1 and 5a simultaneously in awake head-fixed mice undergoing whisker stimulation.
source: Using the double-μPeriscope we measured the axonal activities in cortical layers 1 and 5a simultaneously (Figure 2e) in the awake head-fixed mice undergoing whisker stimulation.
evidence: This describes the experimental setup and is shown in Figure 2e.

claim: All procedures were approved and conducted in accordance with the guidelines given by the veterinary office of Landesamt für Gesundheit und Soziales Berlin (registration number G0278/16).
source: All procedures were approved and conducted in accordance with the guidelines given by the veterinary office of Landesamt für Gesundheit und Soziales Berlin (registration number G0278/16).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval.

source: The age of studied mice was P40–70.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.

source: Both male and female mice were used.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.
